children: Shares in Computacenter rose after the company lifted its full-year guidance on surging first-half pretax profit and revenue, boosted by growth in North America and rising demand for artificial intelligence.
London-listed shares were up 2.9% at 57.60 pounds in morning trade. Year to date, shares have more than doubled.
The FTSE 100 technology and services provider now expects adjusted pretax profit to be significantly ahead of current market expectations and to be no less than 380 million pounds ($514.5 million).
A company-compiled consensus forecasts adjusted pretax profit of 340.9 million pounds with a range of 332.0 million to 354.0 million pounds.
The company had previously said it expected its full-year results to be comfortably ahead of market views.

The raised guidance should drive consensus upgrades to adjusted pretax profit forecasts, J.P. Morgan analysts wrote in a note to clients. The U.S. bank anticipates low-to-mid teens upgrades to consensus adjusted pretax profit forecasts.
Rising demand for artificial intelligence and growth in North America remain the company's key underlying growth drivers, the analysts noted.
First-half revenue rose to 6.845 billion pounds from 3.99 billion pounds, while adjusted operating profit rose to 153.1 million pounds from 82.1 million pounds.

The company's North America business--which now represents more than 60% of group adjusted operating profit-- delivered a record performance, supported by growth in hyperscale, neocloud and enterprise customers leading to further market share gains, the company said.
Meanwhile, pretax profit rose to 142.6 million pounds from 73.2 million pounds.
The company's product order backlog as of June 30 was 9.3 billion pounds, reflecting solid technology sourcing order intake in North America and the U.K.
